overview: 21 official Qs (2008, 2012, 2017, 2024). Delhi Sultanate administration (5) and Mughal administration/society/art (8) dominate; Europeans (3), Cholas, Bhakti-Sufi and Marathas thin. Formats: one-liners on 'who introduced/why', a reform–ruler matching, a 'pair not correctly matched' and a statement set on Mughal painting (all Prelims 2024).

possibility.evidence: 1 Q: 2012; other APPSC exams ask Uttaramerur inscription often
possibility.what_they_ask: Meaning of an administrative term (kadagam = cantonment); natural targets: Uttaramerur (village assemblies), ur/sabha/nagaram, mandalam–valanadu–nadu
Title of a Sultan (Lakh Baksh), purpose of Alauddin's price control, Sultan who set up a PWD, reform–Sultan matching

possibility.angle: Delhi Sultanate socio-economic, religious, art and literature
possibility.what_they_ask: Natural targets in APPSC's who-built / who-wrote style: Qutb Minar (Aibak began, Iltutmish completed), Alai Darwaza, Amir Khusrau, Barani's Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, Ibn Battuta under Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Who introduced the silver rupiya, what Dahsala meant, battle–ruler pair not matched

possibility.angle: Mughal society, economy and religion (incl. Sikh gurus)
possibility.what_they_ask: Founder of the Khalsa, trader class carrying bulk goods (Banjaras), share of produce marketed
Emperor who did not patronise historians/music, incorrect statement on Mughal painting
Order linked with a practice; natural targets: Chishti (Ajmer, sama), Suhrawardi, Naqshbandi orthodoxy
Function of an Ashtapradhan post, who defeated the Marathas at Panipat III
Place where an English fort was built, who framed the Blue Water policy, author of a famous quote on Indian commerce

traps.trap: Reform credited to the neighbouring Sultan [same dynasty swap]
traps.spot: Tughlaq names in options or reform–Sultan matching
traps.fix: Muhammad bin Tughlaq – token currency; Firoz Tughlaq – irrigation canals and PWD; Alauddin – branding of horses; Iltutmish – silver tanka
traps.pyq: 'Muhammad Bin Tughlaq' for PWD → Firoz Tughlaq [prelims-2017#87]; a-II, b-I, c-IV, d-III [prelims-2024#8]

traps.trap: Purpose of a reform replaced by a pleasant-sounding aim
traps.fix: Alauddin fixed prices so a large army could live on low salaries
traps.pyq: 'For better return to the farmers' → soldiers on low salary [prelims-2017#85]

traps.trap: Ten-year average misread as ten-year settlement
traps.fix: Dahsala = cash rates from the average produce and prices of the previous 10 years
traps.pyq: 'standard rate valid for 10 years' → average of last 10 years [prelims-2017#89]

traps.trap: Mughal emperor credited with Sher Shah's measure
traps.spot: Currency/road question with Akbar among options
traps.fix: Silver rupiya and GT Road restoration = Sher Shah Suri

traps.trap: Battle given to the wrong emperor
traps.fix: Chausa 1539 and Bilgram 1540 were Humayun's defeats by Sher Shah; Khanwa = Babur; Haldighati = Akbar

traps.trap: Wrong European agent in a true-sounding statement
traps.spot: Statement on how European art reached the court
traps.fix: Portuguese Jesuits (under Akbar) and English, not Danish merchants

traps.spot: Panipat III with Rohillas/Mughals among options
traps.fix: Ahmad Shah Abdali (Afghan) defeated the Marathas in 1761; Rohillas were his allies
Almeida – Blue Water policy; Albuquerque – capture of Goa 1510

traps.spot: English factory/fort location with Andhra ports
traps.fix: Fort St. George at Madrasapatnam (1639-44); Machilipatnam was the first factory (1611)

techniques.name: Ruler-signature list [one ruler, one signature]
techniques.how: Keep one signature reform per ruler and match: Iltutmish tanka/iqta, Balban sijda, Alauddin dagh/market, MbT token, Firoz canals/PWD, Sher Shah rupiya, Akbar Dahsala/mansab.
techniques.example: Reform matching: token → MbT, dagh → Alauddin, tanka → Iltutmish, irrigation → Firoz → option 2 [prelims-2024#8]

techniques.name: Motive test
techniques.how: For 'why did X do Y', choose the motive tied to the ruler's main problem (Mongol threat → big army → low pay → low prices).
techniques.example: Alauddin's fixed prices → soldiers living on low salary [prelims-2017#85]

techniques.name: Key-word parsing in look-alike options
techniques.how: When all options share a phrase ('10 years'), read what is done with it: average, validity, measurement, sharing.
techniques.example: Dahsala → 'average of produce and prices in the last 10 years' [prelims-2017#89]

techniques.name: Date-chain check for pairs
techniques.how: Place each battle on the timeline with its reign; a battle outside that reign breaks the pair.
techniques.example: Chausa 1539 falls in Humayun's reign, not Jahangir's (1605-27) → pair 4 wrong [prelims-2024#19]

techniques.name: Statement-by-statement for art questions
techniques.how: Verify each statement's actor (who brought whom, which reign); mark only the false one.
techniques.example: Humayun brought Mir Sayyid Ali/Abdus Samad (true); Jahangir golden age (true); Danish merchants (false) → c only [prelims-2024#3]

techniques.name: Office-name decoding
techniques.how: Translate the title: Sar-i-Naubat/Senapati = army chief; Sumant/Dabir = foreign; Amatya = finance.

confusions.remember: Token currency, Diwan-i-Kohi vs canals, PWD, Diwan-i-Khairat
Generosity title vs divine-kingship and 'blood and iron'
Rupiya, GT Road, patta-qabuliyat vs Dahsala, mansabdari
Both Humayun's defeats by Sher Shah
Blue Water policy (1505-09) vs Goa capture (1510)
First English factory on the east coast vs English fort
Bulk long-distance carriers vs bankers/hundi dealers
Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad came under Humayun; peak under Jahangir

anchors: Panipat III, 14 Jan 1761: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeats Marathas
Khalsa founded 1699 by Guru Gobind Singh
Iltutmish: silver tanka and copper jital
Francisco de Almeida: Blue Water policy
Chola 'kadagam' = military cantonment; Uttaramerur = village assemblies
checklist: Which ruler's signature reform is this? Watch same-dynasty swaps
For 'why', pick the motive tied to the ruler's main problem
Place battles and events in the correct reign
Read what is done with a shared key phrase (10 years, silver)
In statement sets, verify the actor in each statement
Victor vs ally; governor vs policy
